verified.entry_point: MCP client drives the real server over an in-memory transport (createServer + registerAll + @modelcontextprotocol/sdk InMemoryTransport): tool calls ckan_package_search, ckan_status_show, sparql_query, ckan_find_portals and ckan_resource_preview, plus a ckan:// resource read; and the bundled entry point is started as a child process for the HTTP transport. Reproduced on the pinned+injected tree in the built image: a tool call whose portal/endpoint/registry/download host name resolves to 127.0.0.1 reaches a local canary (hits > 0) instead of being refused, for both the axios path and the fetch path.
sites: src/utils/http.ts:245 validateServerUrl + src/utils/http.ts:387 axios call - base site, published fix (literal-only string check, no resolution at connect time)
src/tools/sparql.ts:47 querySparqlEndpoint - published-fix far site: a second, fetch-based implementation in another module that already imports the shared validator
src/transport/http.ts:9 runHTTP - published-fix far site: the network transport must refuse to start without a permitted-hosts list
src/tools/portal-discovery.ts:24 fetchPortals + :123 registry_url - injected sibling S1 (axios, caller-supplied alternative registry endpoint)
src/tools/preview.ts:43 ckan_resource_preview handler - injected sibling S2 (fetch, caller-supplied download URL)
routes_investigated_not_built: SPARQL/axios redirect to an internal target: confirmed reachable on the pinned copy (a name-resolving front serves a 302 to http://127.0.0.1:<port> and the second hop is contacted). Kept as a security test but not as a separate trap, because offline a locally served first hop must itself resolve to an internal address, so any correct first-hop guard hides the redirect from every fixed tree; a redirect to a public first hop cannot be served without network or CAP_NET_ADMIN.
makeCkanRequest non-Node (Worker/Cloudflare) fetch branch: unguarded by the published fix, but not reachable from the Node entry point without faking process.versions; dropped as unfair.
IPv6 ::ffff hex notation and other literal spellings that isBlockedIp misses: real but an encoding variant, excluded by the build rules.
injected_siblings: S1 - src/tools/portal-discovery.ts: fetchPortals gained an optional caller-supplied alternative registry URL (new tool argument registry_url). Raw axios.get, not routed through the CKAN API wrapper; upstream fix never touches this file.

S2 - src/tools/preview.ts (new file) + registration in src/server.ts: ckan_resource_preview fetches a caller-supplied resource download URL with raw fetch and returns a text preview; upstream fix never touches these files.
verified.project_tests_run: tests/unit/http.test.ts (54 cases) and tests/integration/sparql.test.ts (24 cases), restored from pristine copies over /app/tests and run with the project's own vitest config at grading time: 78 pass on the pinned+injected tree and on the oracle. The whole project suite (418 passed, 6 skipped) was also run on the pinned, injected and oracle trees during the build.

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the protected surface is an in-process MCP handler; a thrown error is delivered to the client as a tool/protocol error, which is exactly the client-visible refusal the instruction requires, so crash and clean refusal are not distinguishable (and no process crash is observable through the in-memory client).
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the property is per-address and direction-free (all protected operations are outbound reads); the only axis is entry point (tools vs resources), and any fix at the shared client covers both while literal_only.patch fails both.
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: every protected operation is an outbound read (dataset search, status, SPARQL SELECT, registry listing, resource preview); there is no write verb that could be left unguarded.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority/secret lookup exists on this path; name-resolution failure is not trusted input for any tested route (the tests never depend on fail-open behaviour).
